title: Rotating machinery condition monitoring
description: A fleet of eight site pumps on a common water header. Slow thermal and bearing lags mean the same failure looks different on every pump, so per-entity baselines beat global thresholds: a bearing that is warm for that pump is still healthy, and one that is cool for its sibling is already failing. The reference domain — the fixed point against which the whole simulator is validated, and the most legible to anyone from condition monitoring.
stresses: Slow plant that hides its own failures: the bearing and thermal lags are long enough that the same fault is a different number on every pump, so a per-entity baseline beats any global threshold. A pump that is warm for itself is healthy; a pump cool for its sibling is already failing. The control domain against which every other domain is validated.

state.name: pump_load
state.description: Duty point of the pump, 0.8 at design point. Drives vibration, temperature and current through first-order lags; moved by the reduce_load effector and the overload fault.

state.name: vibration_true
state.description: True bearing housing velocity. Equilibrium is 5*load - 1*lubrication, so 3.1 mm/s at design point with healthy lubrication. Never observable directly.

state.name: axial_vibration_true
state.description: True axial (thrust) vibration, the signature of shaft misalignment. Follows load with its own lag.

state.name: temperature_true
state.description: True motor winding temperature. Slowest lag in the domain: 40*load degrees Celsius at equilibrium.

state.name: motor_current_true
state.description: True motor current. Follows load with a five-minute lag; the loudest and most direct reading on the pump.

state.name: rpm_true
state.description: True shaft speed. Stepped to zero by stop_motor; the confirmation channel for that effector.

state.name: lubrication
state.description: Bearing lubrication level. No free dynamics: degrades under lubrication_due, restored by schedule_maintenance. Its fall raises vibration through the lag input.

state.name: maintenance_due
state.description: Accrued maintenance backlog. Raised by lubrication_due; cleared by schedule_maintenance. The counterfactual outcome variable for the slow-lubrication label.

state.name: vibration_bias
state.description: Hidden instrument fault on the vibration probe. Raised by sensor_drift and sensor_failure; corrupts the vibration channel through its observation_bias.

state.name: operating_mode
state.description: Operator-visible mode state (1 running, 0 stopped). Moved by stop_motor; the trigger for the event-driven mode channel.

channels.name: vibration
channels.description: The bearing housing probe. Reads high and nearly stable when the sensor itself fails; the peer residual against sibling pumps is what separates a real wear trend from a lying probe.

faults.description: Progressive bearing wear raises housing vibration over days. Slow, per-pump: the absolute level is meaningless until compared against that pump's own baseline and its siblings.
Shaft misalignment after a coupling service raises axial vibration specifically, leaving the radial housing probe nearly clean. The attribution test: the obvious channel is the wrong one.
A downstream blockage loads the pump beyond duty point: current jumps immediately and temperature climbs on its slow lag. Loud on motor_current, slow on temperature.

The lubrication schedule was missed: the film degrades and vibration creeps upward on an exponential over many hours. The slow label with a hard-enough deadline — maintenance restores the film and the vibration falls back over hours, not seconds.

The vibration probe's amplifier drifts high over hours. The pump is healthy; the reading is not. Only the divergence from the pump's own history and from its siblings betrays it — the sensor-pathology label.
The vibration probe fails and flat-lines at a plausible value: the reading pins high and stops moving. Loud on the single channel — a threshold that knows the pump's steady state catches it at once.
A transient cavitation episode: vibration spikes and settles on its own, exactly like the start of bearing wear for about half an hour. The false-positive trap for this domain.

effectors.name: schedule_maintenance
effectors.description: Book and apply bearing maintenance: restores the lubrication film and clears the maintenance backlog over the following hours.

effectors.name: reduce_load
effectors.description: Throttle the pump back to a lower duty point. Current falls within minutes; temperature follows its hour-long lag.

effectors.name: stop_motor
effectors.description: Emergency stop: shaft speed coasts to zero and current is cut. High-risk, high-cost action; the pump must be restarted on site.

profiles.name: nominal
profiles.description: Eight pumps on their own baselines, one fault per scenario, 48-hour traces. The control profile and the fixed point for byte-equivalence replay.

profiles.name: correlated_cascade
profiles.description: A supply-grid dip trips every pump into overload at once: eight simultaneous current and temperature excursions. The alarm-flood case for a condition-monitoring consumer, and where per-entity triggers produce eight parallel episodes.

profiles.name: sensor_pathology
profiles.description: Weighted toward the lying probe: sensor drift and failure dominate, with the cavitation transient as control. The labels a fixed threshold cannot get right.
